top_choice_rationale: P001 rests on a quantitative prediction (Bistritzer-MacDonald flat bands at a magic angle) that experiment confirmed with correlated insulating and superconducting states, then widely reproduced in many moire platforms; the citation asserts only established observations, not the pairing mechanism, so open mechanism questions do not undermine it. P002 is more mature with a clean two-name credit but is a decisive improvement in a measurement lineage already recognised in 2005 and 2012, so it ranks second. P003 is sound physics but has the weakest credit chain (four candidates for three places, Jaksch omitted) and sits close to earlier prizes, yet I still prefer it to no award because the work is mature and clearly of high quality.
